summary:
Hotar is a cross-platform agricultural decision-support platform (Web, Desktop, and Mobile) that helps farmers adapt to climate change by transforming NASA Earth observation data into actionable, farm-specific crop transition plans.

Powered by a deterministic Rust and WebAssembly physics engine, Hotar fuses 25 years of daily NASA POWER agroclimatology data, NASA MODIS (MOD13Q1) 250m vegetation indices, NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 climate projections through 2100, NASA SRTM 30m topography, and ISRIC SoilGrids 250m soil profiles, validated against 36 years of official county yield records (INS TEMPO and USDA NASS).

When a farmer clicks their parcel on the map, Hotar runs a daily FAO-56 soil-water balance, thermal-stress, and RUSLE erosion simulation alongside a 1,250-path Monte Carlo economic futures model in milliseconds. Instead of complex raw satellite data, farmers receive three tailored 3-year crop rotation strategies filtered by their real machinery, irrigation, and budget constraints—preventing catastrophic drought losses and securing long-term farm profitability and food security.
details:
Hotar is a decision-support app (Web, Desktop, and Mobile) that helps farmers adapt to climate change. Instead of choosing next season’s crops by habit, a farmer clicks their field on the map (or uses GPS in the field) and immediately sees which crops will survive and make money on their exact land over the next 3 to 25 years.

Behind the scenes, Hotar combines 6 real-world data layers:

  1. 25 Years of Daily Weather (NASA POWER): Daily min/max temperatures, rainfall, solar radiation, wind, and root-zone soil moisture from 2001 to 2025.
  2. Future Climate Projections to 2100 (NASA CMIP6): Monthly temperature and rainfall shifts from 5 global climate models under both moderate (SSP2-4.5) and severe (SSP5-8.5) warming scenarios.
  3. Satellite Crop Health (NASA MODIS & GIBS): 25 years of 250-meter satellite vegetation greenness (NDVI) with cloud-filtering, plus live map overlays for soil moisture and land surface temperature.
  4. Real Soil Profiles & Terrain (ISRIC SoilGrids & NASA SRTM): Sand, clay, silt, organic carbon, and pH down to 1 meter deep, paired with 30-meter terrain slope to calculate water retention, surface runoff, and topsoil erosion.
  5. 36 Years of Official Harvest Records (INS TEMPO Romania & USDA): Real county-level yields (tons/hectare) used to validate our simulations against reality.

From Data to a Farm Plan in 50 Milliseconds:

  • Daily Crop Physics: Our engine simulates 12 crops day-by-day across 9,131 days—tracking how much water the soil holds, how much evaporates (FAO-56 water balance), whether heatwaves hit during flowering, and how much topsoil washes away on slopes.
  • 3-Year Rotations & Farm Constraints: Farmers enter their real budget (RON, EUR, or USD), irrigation access, and machinery they already own (planters, drills, combine headers). Hotar filters out crops they cannot afford or harvest, and builds three 3-year crop rotation plans (Conservative, Balanced, and Growth) that naturally restore soil nitrogen and break pest cycles.
  • 2026–2050 Risk Simulation: A 1,250-run Monte Carlo simulation combines future climate droughts with market price swings and fertilizer cost spikes to show the farmer their realistic profit range and worst-case loss risk.
  • Fact-Checked AI Advisor: A built-in Romanian/English AI agronomist explains the recommendation in plain language, while our verification badge automatically checks every number the AI writes against the physics engine so it never hallucinates.

Benefits & Intended Impact

In regions like Southern and Eastern Romania (Bărăgan, Dolj, Vaslui, Teleorman), unirrigated corn has repeatedly collapsed below 1.5–2 tons/hectare during recent summer droughts. Hotar helps farmers transition before going bankrupt—showing them when shifting to drought-tolerant crops like sorghum, sunflower, winter wheat, or chickpeas protects both their income and their topsoil. It also gives agricultural banks and insurers an objective, satellite-backed climate risk score (0–100).

Tools, Coding Languages, & Software Used

  • Simulation Engine: Rust compiled to WebAssembly (WASM)—allowing 25 years of daily physics and 1,250 Monte Carlo futures runs to execute directly inside the browser or offline on a phone in under 50ms.
  • Backend Server: Rust (Axum + Tokio) for live global data fetching when a user clicks any custom location on Earth, plus streaming AI responses.
  • Frontend & Maps: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and MapLibre GL with interactive NASA satellite layers and custom SVG charts.
  • Desktop & Mobile: Tauri v2 (native desktop app) and Capacitor (mobile app with field GPS).
  • Data Pipeline: Python scripts (numpy, requests) to process and clean satellite, soil, climate, and national statistics datasets.

What Makes Hotar Creative

  • Two Views in One App: A simple Farmer View focused on money per hectare, required equipment, and clear advice, and a Science View for agronomists showing daily soil moisture curves, satellite correlations, and model accuracy metrics.
  • "Drought Replay" (2022 & 2024): Farmers rarely trust abstract 2050 graphs, so we built a replay mode that re-runs the real 2022 and 2024 summer droughts day-by-day on their soil—visually proving how drought-resistant crops survive when traditional corn fails.
